facts.raw_span: history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps
4 weeks of bloody and watery diarrhea
6 × 7-cm well-demarcated vegetative crusted plaques on the bilateral cheeks
Intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration and intracorneal neutrophils
Septal panniculitis with Miescher radial granulomas
history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of facial crusted plaques, fever, and neutrophilic inflammation on biopsy is consistent with Sweet syndrome.
The patient's history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps, along with bloody and watery diarrhea, suggests inflammatory bowel disease.
The patient's presentation of painful subcutaneous nodules and septal panniculitis with Miescher radial granulomas on biopsy is consistent with erythema nodosum.
The patient's presentation of facial crusted plaques and intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration on biopsy is consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.
The patient's presentation of facial crusted plaques and neutrophilic inflammation on biopsy is consistent with neutrophilic dermatosis.

rationales.F05: Facial crusted plaques are a characteristic feature of Sweet syndrome and neutrophilic dermatosis.
rationales.F08: Well-demarcated vegetative crusted plaques on the cheeks are typical of Sweet syndrome and neutrophilic dermatosis.
rationales.F11: Intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration and intracorneal neutrophils is a hallmark of Sweet syndrome and neutrophilic dermatosis.
rationales.F02: History of diverticulosis and colonic polyps increases the likelihood of inflammatory bowel disease and pyoderma gangrenosum.
rationales.F06: Bloody and watery diarrhea is a common symptom of inflammatory bowel disease and pyoderma gangrenosum.
rationales.F12: Septal panniculitis with Miescher radial granulomas is a characteristic feature of erythema nodosum.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of facial crusted plaques, well-demarcated vegetative crusted plaques, and intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration supports Sweet syndrome, which is further strengthened by the absence of wound culture growth and the presence of mild leukocytosis with a normal differential.
